messages:
incidents-bot: [PAGER] Sev 2 - High error rate for tenant Seraphim (dedicated VPC/east-west) in eu-west-1. Symptoms: 5xx spike, ~40% request failures, latency > 2s. Pager: @pager_elena 

pager_elena: acked. pulling logs from the pool, @oncall-marc are you free to take primary? I'll join for comms with Seraphim. 

oncall-marc: taking. status channel for runbook is #incidents. quick recap: customer on dedicated GPU pool in eu-west-1, sudden 5xx across multiple endpoints since ~1807554200. Cause unknown. 

sre-lin: I'm seeing KV cache thrashing and backend gRPC timeouts to model shards in pool-3-eu-west. CPU/GPU utilization looks normal but network retransmits up. Possibly a regional networking flap. 

eng-platform-raj: Confirmed we have BGP churn to the colo — routing team reports flaps 1807553500-1807554100. Could be intermittent connectivity to the dedicated pool. 

dns-ops-amy: Noted. TTL for Seraphim custom DNS is 300s. We can lower to 30s before cutover if we need to shift traffic. Need approval from acctmgr-team and customer for low TTL. 

acctmgr-kate: Looping in Seraphim. @cust-success-james please call them and tell them we're preparing a regional reroute. 

cust-success-james: On call with Seraphim now. They see 502s in eu-west and confirm they can tolerate a controlled cutover to eu-central-1 for up to 2 hours. They want zero data loss and minimal timeout errors. 

oncall-marc: Plan proposal: 1) Warm dedicated pool in eu-central-1 (reserve same instance types), 2) Sync KV/cache state (prefix-based warm cache), 3) Reduce DNS TTL to 30, 4) Perform DNS cutover with phased weights (traffic-split 90/10 -> 50/50 -> 0/100) using weighted DNS, 5) Monitor SLOs and rollback if errors > 5%. Need ops confirm for warm capacity + time estimates. 

eng-platform-raj: We can spin identical dedicated pool in eu-central-1. ETA to warm with images and model artifacts (quantized) = ~22 minutes. Network peerings for VPC will take extra 12 minutes for routes and firewall rules. Total ~35-40m. 

sre-lin: For cache sync, we can use prefix snapshot tool to copy hot prefixes from eu-west to eu-central. This will take ~8 minutes. We'll throttle to avoid backend overload. 

dns-ops-amy: I can lower TTL now to 30s, will push change to Seraphim delegated zone. need explicit go from customer via @cust-success-james. 

cust-success-james: SeraphimOps on the call: "Go ahead for TTL change and warm in eu-central-1. We'll accept phased shift and will pause traffic if errors spike." They asked that we keep them updated on each weight step. 

oncall-marc: ok lowering TTL. dns-ops-amy: proceed. 

dns-ops-amy: TTL lowered to 30s for *.seraphim.internal by 1807554620. propagation check: dig shows TTL=30 from our public resolvers. 

eng-platform-raj: Kicking off pool spin in eu-central-1 at 1807554705. Using reserved images and the same dedicated pool config (pool-seraphim-dedicated-v2). 

sre-lin: Starting prefix snapshot transfer at 1807554780 -> copying hot prefixes via snapshot tool. Will monitor transfer rates. 

oncall-marc: good. Eng-raj, what's our expected moment when the pool is ready to accept traffic? 

eng-platform-raj: Pool pass health checks at 1807554860 (all node agents green). Model load complete at 1807554925. Ready to receive validation traffic. 

sre-lin: Cache sync completed at 1807554948. Ran small validation run: 100 sample requests, 0 errors, latency in target range. 

oncall-marc: Starting phased DNS traffic shift. Step 1: weighted DNS 90% eu-west / 10% eu-central at 1807555000. dns-ops-amy to apply record changes. 

dns-ops-amy: Applied weighted records: seraphim.api -> 90% eu-west, 10% eu-central at 1807555007. Control plane shows weight applied. 

incidents-bot: [ANOMALY] After step 1, overall error rate dropped from 40% -> 28% in 10 minutes. eu-west still seeing errors but eu-central healthy. 

cust-success-james: Seraphim: "We're seeing a reduction but still some spikes. Keep shifting." They ask if we can accelerate. 

oncall-marc: We'll go to 50/50 after 6 minutes if metrics stable. SLO threshold to proceed: 5xx < 15% and p95 latency <1.5s. 

sre-lin: At 1807555320 5xx=12% overall, p95=1.3s. Go to 50/50 now. 

dns-ops-amy: Changed weights to 50/50 at 1807555335. TTL ensures clients pick up change quickly. 

incidents-bot: [STATUS] 15 minutes into cutover. Overall 5xx now 6%, eu-west 10%, eu-central 2%. No degradation in model outputs. 

cust-success-james: Seraphim confirms traffic looks normal on their dashboards. "Nice work. Please continue to 0/100 when safe." 

oncall-marc: We'll prepare final cutover but hold until eu-west error floor stabilizes below 5% for 5 minutes. Current eu-west 7% at 1807555450. 

sre-lin: We also found a correlated NAT gateway saturation causing retransmits in eu-west. We're scaling NAT gateways and rerouting control plane to avoid the saturated path. This should finish in ~6 minutes. 

eng-platform-raj: NAT scaling complete at 1807555508. Control-plane retransmits down to baseline. eu-west 5xx trending down. 

oncall-marc: Good. Proceed to 0/100 cutover at 1807555550. dns-ops-amy apply. 

dns-ops-amy: Applied final cutover seraphim.api -> 100% eu-central at 1807555556. 

incidents-bot: [RESOLUTION] After final cutover, overall 5xx < 1% and p95 latency 0.9s. Customer traffic now fully served from eu-central-1 dedicated pool. 

cust-success-james: Seraphim: "All green. No errors observed. Thank you." They request a short post-incident note and timeline. 

oncall-marc: We'll keep the eu-west pool on standby (warm) for 2 hours then drain if stable. Also opening a follow-up action item: investigate root cause of NAT gateway saturation and BGP flaps in eu-west. 

sre-lin: I'll own RCA for networking and NAT sizing. eng-platform-raj will document improvements for pool failover automation (faster warmup, pre-synced cache). 

acctmgr-kate: I'll coordinate customer billing/credits and share the postmortem with Seraphim legal as requested. 

incidents-bot: Incident closed at 1807556123 by oncall-marc. Postmortem requested and assigned: RCA owners: sre-lin, eng-platform-raj. 

oncall-marc: Quick notes for postmortem: timeline, decision to warm eu-central, TTL lowering, phased weighted DNS cutover, final closure. Attach logs and sample queries. Thanks all for rapid response :thumbsup: 

seraphim-ops: "Appreciate the clear comms and the quick cutover. We'll review the postmortem and schedule a follow-up to discuss durable multi-region setup."
